transcript.text: Bosch built-in microwave BFL524MS0B randomly stops part way through cooking, time still on the display. Opening and closing the door lets it carry on. Maybe once every few days.

This behaviour—where the microwave stops but the clock keeps running, and restarting happens after you open and close the door—is a common sign of an intermittent fault in the door interlock system. The microwave has safety switches that cut power if it thinks the door is opening; if those switches are worn or the latch isn't engaging perfectly, it cuts out mid-cycle. The most common causes are:
1. Debris in the latch: Food grease or crumbs getting into the plastic hooks on the door edge can stop them from clicking fully home.
2. Worn interlock switch: The electrical switches inside the housing may be failing to maintain contact when the door is closed.
3. Loose wiring: A wire at the door hinge might be loose and only making contact when the door is moved. To help narrow this down, please unplug the microwave first for safety. Then check the plastic hooks on the door edge and the slots they engage with. Is there any visible grease or debris in those areas? Also, do the plastic hooks look intact (not cracked or broken), or do they look damaged?

There was some grease around the door hooks and latch slots, so I cleaned it off. It still happened once since. I can't see any cracked or broken hooks as far as I can tell. No smell, sparks or tripping either.

Since cleaning the latch didn't stop it from cutting out, and there are no obvious cracks in the plastic hooks, the issue is likely electrical rather than mechanical. The most probable cause now is a worn door interlock switch inside the housing that loses contact intermittently when the microwave vibrates or heats up. Are any of these wires frayed, loose in their clips, or disconnected? If the wiring looks fine and it continues to stop randomly, the interlock switch itself is likely faulty. Because this involves opening the casing near high-voltage components, I'd recommend calling an engineer to check the switch safely.

candidates: Door interlock or latch mechanism fault (high)
Loose internal wiring at the door hinges (medium)
